sources.citation: Agostiniani, Luciano. 2006. "Epigrafia e lingua elime: un bilancio". In Guerra e pace in Sicilia e nel Mediterraneo antico (VIII-III sec. a.C.). Arte, prassi e teoria della pace e della guerra. Atti delle quinte giornate internazionali di studi sull'area elima e la Sicilia occidentale nel contesto mediterraneo (Erice, 12-15 ottobre 2003), vol. II, 683-688. Pisa: Edizioni della Normale.
sources.note: Nothing on accent. Content: Elymian is IE and flexional; Ambrosini/Georgiev Anatolian theses rejected; Lejeune's Italic thesis rests on saritu-/peiie-; 'points of no return': Selinuntine alphabet with reversed-N = /b/, ordinary beta = a labial fricative /f/ or /phi/; nominatives in -a, datives in -ai with emi ('atai tukai emi'), coin legend Segestazib emi = dat. pl. < *-bhi; refutation of Marchesini 1998 (reversed-N as mis-executed ny); the -a + emi formula in new graffiti (*382, *385) read as nominative or as a Greek genitive on a local name.

sources.citation: Arena, Renato. 1997. "Della possibile presenza di forme elime in documenti epigrafici greci". In Seconde Giornate Internazionali di Studi sull'Area Elima (Gibellina, 22-26 ottobre 1994). Atti, vol. I, 77-84. Pisa-Gibellina: Scuola Normale Superiore / CESDAE.
sources.note: Nothing on Elymian accent (searched and skimmed): Greek EIMI vs EMI spellings, dative dedications, onomastics.

sources.citation: Biondi, Laura. 1997. "Nuovi frammenti ceramici graffiti da Segesta". In Seconde Giornate Internazionali di Studi sull'Area Elima (Gibellina, 22-26 ottobre 1994). Atti, vol. I, 141-162. Pisa-Gibellina: Scuola Normale Superiore / CESDAE.
sources.note: No rule or statement of word accent. The only accent-adjacent words found anywhere in the Elymian literature opened: arguing against the apocope of final -i in -b < *-bhi, Biondi notes that final -i is preserved 'in emi (sebbene qui presumibilmente essa sia tonica)' -- a parenthetical assumption that the final vowel of the one verb form emi 'I am' carries the accent (page scan checked); footnote 18 concerns the Erycine spelling -aziib, not accent. Rest of the paper: morphology of -a / -a(a)i / -azib (read as genitives), formulae of possession, coin legends.

sources.citation: Agostiniani, Luciano. 1992. "L'elimo nel quadro linguistico della Sicilia anellenica". In Giornate Internazionali di Studi sull'Area Elima (Gibellina, 19-22 settembre 1991). Atti, vol. I, 1-11. Pisa-Gibellina: Scuola Normale Superiore / CESDAE.
sources.note: Nothing on accent (scanned of all 13 content pages searched for accent|prosod|sillab|tonic|quantit|vocal; only 'tratti fonetici' of the Mendolito Sikel texts). Content: glosses, toponymy and anthroponymy of the Elymian area, composite nature of the Segesta graffiti corpus, the secure linguistic facts (emi 1sg 'to be', dat. sg. -ai of possession, nom. sg. -a), beta of the coin legends as a labial fricative -> dat. pl. from *-bhi; conclusion 'l'italicita dell'elimo e possibile.. probabile, ma resta ancora in larga misura ipotetica'.

sources.citation: Nenci, Giuseppe. 1992. 'Elimi'. In Enciclopedia Italiana di Scienze, Lettere ed Arti, V Appendice. Roma: Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana (online edition at treccani.it; section 'Alfabeto e lingua degli Elimi').
sources.note: No phonology content. The language paragraph says only that Elymian is attested epigraphically by ceramic graffiti (Segesta, Entella, Monte Castellazzo di Poggioreale, Montelepre), that the alphabet resembles that of Selinus, and reports classification opinions: 'una generica indoeuropeita' (Agostiniani), 'origine balcanico-anatolica' (Durante), 'elementi chiaramente anatolici' (Ambrosini); bibliography Durante 1961, Ambrosini 1970, Agostiniani 1977.

sources.citation: Lejeune, Michel. 1969. "La langue élyme d'après les graffites de Ségeste (Ve siècle)". Comptes rendus des séances de l'Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres 113(2): 237-242. DOI 10.3406/crai.1969.12378.
sources.note: Phonology content is limited to segmental/comparative remarks (p.241-242): Elymian is Indo-European (emi 'je suis'), 'une langue centum (occlusives p, t, k; b, d, g) à cinq timbres vocaliques (c'est-à-dire sans confusions de o et a)', with conservation of initial *s- (and probably *y-) before vowel; script is dextroverse Greek alphabet without word separation. Nothing on accent, stress or quantity; the corpus (abbreviated names, datives in -ai/-oi/-ei, a few verb forms) carries no accent notation.

sources.citation: Kinch, K. F. 1888. 'Die Sprache der sicilischen Elymer'. Zeitschrift fuer Numismatik 16: 187-207. Berlin: Weidmann.
sources.note: No prosodic content (searched Beton-/Accent/Akzent/Ton/Silbe/Quantit- over pp.187-207 and read the phonetic passages in context). Content: dating of the legend series against the Selinuntine/Megarian alphabet; the value of B as an e-vowel ('das B sei hier als Vokal aufzufassen'), a glide j developing between i and a following vowel (Irykazije, with Cypriot/Pamphylian/Lycian parallels), the ethnic suffix -azi- and the endings -B/-IA/-IE/-ION compared with Greek dialect forms; conclusion that the language stood close to an Ionic Greek dialect. Nothing on word accent.
